participants: Andrew Musial (closer, labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' in the transcript)
summary: Roughly a 41-minute manager one-to-one that contains almost no sales content. Chris opens by congratulating Andrew on another paid-in-full close that day and confirms the $50,000 monthly commitment is on track, then hands the agenda over. Andrew spends the first twenty minutes describing a year-long personal journey through a three-part men's workshop series called The Man's Path, including a period of sustained unemployment and severe self-doubt after being laid off from a previous sales role, funding a sales mentorship out of savings he had promised himself he would not touch, and arriving at a decision to buy a home and start a family. Chris responds with extended non-dual spiritual coaching — intention versus attachment, the ego as the source of suffering, 'who or what is aware', and the proposition that nothing has inherent meaning. Andrew signals discomfort with that direction three separate times and Chris continues each time. The final five minutes translate the philosophy into sales terms: detach from the outcome, serve from love, and paradoxically close more because you are present to the person rather than to the sale. Chris recommends the book Letting Go and closes.
notable: SALES PHILOSOPHY STATED, and it contradicts the same manager's coaching the previous day. Here: 'somebody who doesn't care whether somebody closes or not, or has no worth about this person closing or not, can sit there in objections and be like, what's going on? What's going on for you?... Because they have no care about the sale.' In the 06/22 team meeting the same manager said 'I don't let them get off the phone' and endorsed a rep's view that he should have pushed harder on a prospect who wanted to consult his partner.

The rep discloses a recent extended period of severe psychological distress following a layoff — 'it got me to a really bad, bad spot. Really bad spot' and 'I'm terrible. I cannot do this... I'm not made for this' — inside a recorded and retained call with his direct manager.
The rep discloses repeated psychedelic drug use and a holotropic breathing vision state on the same recording.

The rep discloses personal financial strain: he funded a sales mentorship in late February from savings and investments he had committed never to touch, then was laid off from the offer he joined roughly a month later for non-performance, with 'no actually, no help from the sales manager or so ever'. This is direct context for how to read his ramp-up period in this corpus.

Andrew asks Chris to stop the philosophical line three times — 'Let's leave it like this for today', 'Don't get me in a state that I will say, this is all worthless', and 'You don't want to get me in a hairy state' — and the conversation continues past each.

Chris's reply 'I didn't put Harry in that state' is ambiguous. It reads as either a pun on the rep's phrase or a reference to Harry Edmonds, the closer confirmed as having left the team in the 06/22 meeting. Worth a human check.
Confirms a second paid-in-full close by Andrew on 2026-06-23 — 'great job getting another piffy today' — which should reconcile against the two undated 06/23 prospect calls in this batch.
Confirms the monthly commitment structure is being tracked personally: 'Getting to that 50k as, as promised.'
No recording disclosure or consent appears anywhere in the transcript despite the depth of personal material covered.
